lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's joyful greeting captures Elizabeth's tenderness from the very start.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert's kiss and shortened visits show his devotion before they can be together.

lines.text: May God bless you, dearest beloved, I love, love you!
lines.note: Her declaration of love anchors the early exchange.

lines.text: But if one heart and one life will do, ... they are yours ...
lines.note: Her promise of one heart and one life is the emotional core of the first quarter.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Flush's sudden disappearance becomes a shared crisis and private joke.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Robert's sympathy for poor Flush shows his care for Elizabeth's companion.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth's playful Flush parallel turns their danger into intimacy.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush found and lying on the sofa gives the reunion its vivid, comic relief.

lines.text: I am delighted to know Flush is with you, if I am not.
lines.note: Robert's delight that Flush is with Elizabeth, even if he is not, keeps their bond alive.

lines.text: I went out in the carriage and bought a pair of boots for Italy, besides the shoes—because, you see, we shall have such long walks in the forest after the camels, and it won’t do to go in one’s slippers.
lines.note: Her practical boots for Italy show her readiness for their shared journey.

lines.text: And then, you shall have the ring ... soon enough and safer.
lines.note: The ring promise marks the move from secret courtship to commitment.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Her brief word after the wedding carries the relief and wonder of the day.

lines.text: Bless you, my very own, only Ba—my pride, and joy, and utter comfort.
lines.note: Robert's pride and joy in Elizabeth crowns the final quarter.

lines.text: I can bring you no flowers but I pluck this bud and send it with all affectionate devotion.
lines.note: The small bud he sends is a tender keepsake from their last letters.
